fieldMarks: Long-necked and long-legged, chestnut, gray and black, with a bright pink bill
Large white wing patch striking in flight
Sexes similar; young have a gray bill and muted colours
behavior: Gregarious; not strongly migratory, and flocks disappear from some northern breeding areas in winter
Forages much on land, by day or night, on waste grain in harvested fields and on prairies; wades or dabbles in shallow water
Eats mostly seeds and grains; invertebrates under 10% of diet
Mellow whistling calls; nests in tree cavities, nest boxes or on the ground, often in colonies
habitat: Shallow ponds and fresh marshes, favoring ponds surrounded by trees; forages in dry fields and irrigated land.
range: Resident from southern Arizona and southeastern Texas south through Middle and South America; possibly expanding into eastern Texas and southwestern Louisiana; small flocks may wander well north of the normal range.
